item.title: HugeGraph Java Client
item.description:
1 Overview

HugeGraph Java Client translates Java APIs into REST requests to HugeGraph Server. It supports managing schemas and graph data, executing Gremlin queries, and calling Traverser APIs. This guide covers quick-start setup and examples alongside complete core API reference documentation.

For other languages, use the Go Client or the Python Client.

2 What You Need

  • JDK 17 for this walkthrough and for building Client 1.8.0 from Toolchain master
  • Maven 3.6.3+

item.title: HugeGraph Python Client Quick Start
item.description:
hugegraph-python-client is the Python SDK for Apache HugeGraph. It provides schema management, graph data manipulation, Gremlin execution, real-time traversals, and asynchronous whole-graph computing. HugeGraph-LLM and HugeGraph-ML also use this client for database operations.

The client source code is hosted in the hugegraph-ai repository under hugegraph-python-client/. The import package name is pyhugegraph.

Requirements

  • Python >= 3.12 (Python 3.12–3.14 supported).
  • HugeGraph Server 1.5.0 or later (Server 1.7+ recommends GraphSpace mode; 1.5/1.6 uses legacy routing).
  • pip or uv package manager.

Runtime dependencies include decorator, requests, urllib3, and rich.

item.title: HugeGraph Go Client Quick Start
item.description:
HugeGraph Go Client is the Go SDK in the Toolchain repository. It currently provides APIs for version queries, schemas (property keys, vertex labels, and edge labels), vertices, and Gremlin. An edge data API is not implemented yet.

This module is still under development. Refer to the source code under hugegraph-client-go/api/v1 for the currently available interfaces.

Requirements

  • Go 1.19 or later
  • An accessible HugeGraph Server; examples use http://127.0.0.1:8080
